options.option_text: Classroom (classroom is where teaching happens, but not the institution)
School (correct: a doctor works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school ✓)
Student (student is who teacher teaches, not where they work)
Education (education is a broader concept, not a workplace)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: professional → their workplace. Doctor works in a Hospital; Teacher works in a School. The analogy is: Person → Institution/Place of work.

options.option_text: Vein (vein carries blood; ink doesn't 'carry' a pen — relationship is wrong)
Body (body contains blood; but pen doesn't contain ink — pen uses ink)
Heart (correct: as ink is to a pen (the fluid that makes it work), blood is to the heart (the fluid that the heart pumps) ✓)
Plasma (plasma is a component of blood, not what blood is to the heart)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Relationship: Ink is the fluid that the pen uses/pumps. Blood is the fluid that the Heart pumps. Ink : Pen = Blood : Heart (fluid → pump analogy).

options.option_text: Volume (kilogram measures mass/weight, not volume)
Speed (kilogram doesn't measure speed)
Weight/Mass (correct: kilometre measures distance; kilogram measures weight/mass ✓)
Time (kilogram doesn't measure time)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Relationship: unit → what it measures. Kilometre measures Distance; Kilogram measures Weight/Mass. Unit-to-measurement analogies are very common in SSC exams.

options.option_text: Artist (artist creates a painting; book doesn't create a library)
Gallery (correct: books are collected and displayed in a library; paintings are collected and displayed in a gallery ✓)
Canvas (canvas is what a painting is made on; not the collection place)
Exhibition (an exhibition is an event, not a permanent collection place)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: item → place where it is collected/kept/displayed. Books are kept in a Library; Paintings are kept in a Gallery (also called an art gallery or museum).

options.option_text: Ocean (ocean is the natural habitat; aviary is an enclosure for birds, not just habitat)
Aquarium (correct: an aviary is an enclosure for birds; an aquarium is an enclosure/tank for fish ✓)
Fins (fins are body parts of fish; feathers are to birds)
River (river is natural habitat; aviary is a human-made enclosure)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: animal → enclosed dwelling. Aviary = a large cage or enclosure for birds. Aquarium = a tank or enclosed area for fish. Other animal enclosures: kennel (dogs), stable (horses), apiary (bees), pen (sheep), sty (pigs).

options.option_text: Kidney (nephrology studies kidney, not neurology)
Bone (orthopaedics studies bones)
Brain/Nervous system (correct: cardiologist specialises in the heart; neurologist specialises in the brain and nervous system ✓)
Eyes (ophthalmology studies eyes, not neurology)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Relationship: specialist → their field of medicine. Cardiologist → Heart. Neurologist → Brain/Nervous system. Medical speciality vocabulary: cardiologist (heart), neurologist (nervous system), dermatologist (skin), ophthalmologist (eyes), nephrologist (kidneys), orthopaedist (bones).

options.option_text: Metal (an axe can cut metal but that's not its primary use)
Wood (correct: scissors are used to cut cloth; an axe is used to cut wood ✓)
Iron (iron is material, not the thing an axe typically cuts)
Sharpen (sharpen is the action, not the object cut by the axe)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: tool → material it cuts. Scissors cut Cloth; Axe cuts Wood. Analogy type: tool-material pairs.

options.option_text: Same (same = identical; not the precise opposite of similar in meaning)
Different/Dissimilar (correct: synonymous means 'same meaning'; antonymous means 'opposite meaning'; similarly, similar means 'alike', so the opposite is dissimilar ✓)
Related (related doesn't mean opposite)
Parallel (parallel doesn't mean opposite of similar)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: word → its opposite. Synonymous is to Antonymous (same meaning : opposite meaning). Similar : Dissimilar (alike : unlike). The pattern is X : Opposite of X.

options.option_text: Blood pressure (blood pressure is a measurement, not the missing substance in anaemia)
Haemoglobin/Iron (correct: dehydration is deficiency of water; anaemia is deficiency of haemoglobin (caused by iron deficiency) ✓)
Oxygen (low oxygen is hypoxia, not anaemia, though anaemia reduces oxygen-carrying capacity)
Glucose (low glucose is hypoglycaemia, not anaemia)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: condition → the thing that is deficient. Dehydration = deficiency of Water. Anaemia = deficiency of Haemoglobin/Iron (insufficient red blood cells/haemoglobin). Medical deficiency analogies: scurvy (Vitamin C), rickets (Vitamin D/calcium), kwashiorkor (protein), goitre (iodine).

options.option_text: 400 m (400 m is a middle-distance event, sometimes called a sprint but technically separate)
100 m (correct: a marathon is the longest standard running event at 42.195 km; a sprint commonly refers to the 100 m event ✓)
1500 m (1500 m is middle-distance, not a sprint)
5000 m (5000 m is long-distance, not a sprint)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: event name → distance. Marathon covers 42.195 km. Sprint (100 m dash) covers 100 m. The marathon is the longest standard Olympic running race; the 100 m sprint is the shortest and the 'blue riband' event of sprinting.
